To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) DNA shape is a direct and separate component of binding site recognition by Hox transcription factors; 2) Hox proteins can be engineered to change their DNA binding preferences in vitro and in vivo, and this can be used as a tool to study the role of DNA shape in gene regulation; 3) DNA shape features can be used to improve binding site prediction by transcription factors.
the recognition of DNA shape is an independent mode of recognition by Hox proteins and that the accuracy of Hox-DNABinding Specificity predictions is improved by adding shape features.
(i) DNA shape is an important determinant of binding specificity of the Hox proteins, and (ii) the recognition of DNA shape by Hox proteins can be deconvoluted from the recognition of the DNA bases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which DNA sequence and shape contribute to protein-DNA interactions.
the recognition of DNA shape and its role in transcriptional regulation.
the molecular recognition of the DNA molecule by proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recognition of the DNA shape is a direct and important component of the binding specificity of the Hox proteins.
the recognition of DNA shape is not only important, but also an independent mode of recognition.
the DNA shape recognition is a direct component of binding site recognition by Hox proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shape of the DNA is an important factor in Hox protein-DNA interactions.
we can now separate the sequence and shape recognition components of protein-DNA binding.
DNA shape is a direct and important determinant of Hox binding site selection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA shape recognition by proteins is an independent mode of DNA binding that is not mediated by sequence.
the recognition of DNA shape by transcription factors can be dissociated from sequence recognition.
the recognition of DNA shape is a general mechanism of protein-DNA recognition, which can be exploited to predict protein binding sites in the genome.
